title: Formatting help
intro: The editor combines several languages: Markdown for text, LaTeX for formulas, and specialized code blocks for diagrams, figures, timelines and other content.

markdown.title: Markdown
markdown.heading: Headings, from largest to smallest
markdown.table: Table: a header row, a separator row, then the data rows.
markdown.resourceNote: To insert a library file (image, audio, video, document), use the “Insert a resource” button below the editor: the link stays valid over time, unlike a URL pasted by hand.

callouts.title: Callouts
callouts.intro: A quote whose first line is a marker becomes a colored box: [!DEFINITION], [!RETENIR] (key point), [!METHODE] (method), [!EXEMPLE] (example), [!REMARQUE] (note) or [!ATTENTION] (warning); the GitHub keywords NOTE, TIP, IMPORTANT, WARNING and CAUTION work too. Text after the marker replaces the title; a blank line ends the callout.

latex.title: Formulas (LaTeX)
latex.intro: Rendered by KaTeX. An invalid formula shows in red without breaking the rest of the block.
latex.block: Centered formula, on its own line

mhchem.title: Chemistry (mhchem)
mhchem.intro: Inside a formula, \ce{…} writes a chemical equation (automatic subscripts, charges and arrows) and \pu{…} a quantity with its unit.

mermaid.title: Diagrams (Mermaid)
mermaid.intro: Describe a diagram in a code block tagged “mermaid”; it is rendered automatically in the preview.
mermaid.types: Mermaid also supports sequence diagrams, Gantt charts, pie charts and many more.
mermaid.mathNote: LaTeX (`$…$`) is not rendered inside Mermaid nodes: put your formulas in the text, around the diagram.

geogebra.title: GeoGebra activities
geogebra.intro: Embeds an activity published on geogebra.org: provide its identifier in a “geogebra” code block.

jsxgraph.title: Dynamic figures (JSXGraph)
jsxgraph.intro: Plots interactive curves and points from equations, in a “jsxgraph” code block.

tikz.title: Figures (TikZ)
tikz.intro: Draws precise vector diagrams in LaTeX/TikZ inside a “tikz” code block; the figure is compiled in the browser.

timeline.title: Timelines
timeline.intro: Place periods (period=start,end,label) and events (event=date,label) on a time axis, in a “timeline” code block; negative years are BC.

smiles.title: Molecules (SMILES)
smiles.intro: Draws the skeletal formula of one molecule per line, in SMILES notation, in a “smiles” code block; an optional caption follows a vertical bar |.

vegalite.title: Charts (Vega-Lite)
vegalite.intro: Draws a data chart (bars, lines, points, pies…) described in Vega-Lite JSON in a “vegalite” code block; the data goes in data.values.

abc.title: Sheet music (ABC)
abc.intro: Engraves a tune written in ABC notation (headers X:, T:, M:, L:, K: then the notes) in an “abc” code block; it plays on the piano in one click.

sql.title: Runnable SQL
sql.intro: An “sql” code block becomes an SQLite query that students run and edit; the database setup comes before a -- @query line.

python.title: Runnable Python
python.intro: A “python” code block becomes a program that students run and edit in their browser; numpy and matplotlib are available, input() reads the Inputs field.

passage.title: Numbered-line texts
passage.intro: A “passage” code block shows an excerpt to study, one source line per line of text, numbered in the margin every five lines; blank lines are not counted.
